audit_findings.title: The anchor may rely on an abnormally low R&D run-rate
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2026 R&D was $11.2 million, $17.8 million below FY2025 and $19.1 million below FY2024; any required normalization is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: A recurring R&D shortfall would reduce anchor OE and the cash flows grown from it.
audit_findings.evidence: Our research and development expenses were $ 11.2 million, $ 29.0 million and $ 30.3 million for fiscal 2026, 2025 and 2024, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The spending decline is demonstrated, but the record does not establish whether it reflects durable efficiency, reclassification, deferred work, or underinvestment. The $17.8 million year-over-year gap equals 28.6% of the $62.3 million anchor, so a substantial recurring restoration could alter the valuation, but no supportable adjustment is presently established.
audit_findings.action: Obtain management's explanation and an R&D reconciliation by function and account; determine normalized recurring R&D and rerun all scenarios if a restoration is supported.

audit_findings.title: Removal of the nonrecurring NMTC gain is not demonstrated
audit_findings.magnitude: $6.740 million pretax, equal to 10.8% of the $62.3 million OE anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: If retained, the nonrecurring other-income gain inflates anchor OE and every forecast cash flow derived from it.
audit_findings.evidence: During fiscal 2026, we settled our final two NMTC transactions, which resulted in recognizing benefits of $ 6.7 million in other (income) expense, net.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that the final NMTC settlement produced a nonrecurring $6.740 million gain. It does not demonstrate that the OE worksheet removed the gain. Inclusion is therefore an unresolved calculation error, but its potential scale is material because the base value of $39.87 already has essentially no cushion to the $39.97 market price.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $6.740 million gain and its specific tax effect through the OE worksheet; if included, remove both and rerun the valuation.

audit_findings.title: Contract-estimate profits could reverse
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2026 net favorable catch-up adjustments were $8.832 million pretax, or 14.2% of anchor OE; Q1 FY2027 recorded a $0.669 million net unfavorable adjustment
audit_findings.mechanism: Estimate revisions enter operating income and OE; later cost overruns or reduced contract consideration reverse previously recognized profit and lower future OE.
audit_findings.evidence: Due to the significant judgments utilized in our revenue recognition on long-term contracts, if subsequent actual results and/or updated assumptions, estimates, or projections were to materially change from those utilized at February 28, 2026, our results of operations in the future could be materially impacted.
audit_findings.explanation: The FY2026 favorable contribution was large relative to the anchor, and the following quarter provides filed evidence of a partial reversal, although not evidence that the full FY2026 amount will reverse. Because the base valuation is approximately equal to market price, a material normalization of these profits could change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Review project-level estimate-at-completion histories, change-order enforceability, retainage and collections, loss-contract provisions, and subsequent catch-up adjustments; rerun using any demonstrated recurring or reversed amount.

audit_findings.title: The pending acquisition can invalidate the as-filed claim perimeter
audit_findings.magnitude: GroGlass terms are unquantified; the supplied 10-Q separately reports KCI consideration of approximately $105 million cash plus up to $10 million earn-out
audit_findings.mechanism: Closing can change acquired OE, cash, debt, assumed liabilities, transaction costs, and potentially diluted shares, making the current numerator, bridge, and denominator stale.
audit_findings.evidence: As we consider and execute acquisitions, we may incur the following risks, among others: difficulties with integrating operations, technologies, products, and employees; failing to realize expected revenue growth and cost synergies from integration initiatives; increasing debt levels to finance an acquisition; failing to fully anticipate changes in cash flows or other market-based assumptions or conditions that cause the value of acquired assets to fall below book value, requiring impairment of intangible assets including goodwill; identifying contingent liabilities subsequent to closing an acquisition; and entering markets in which we have no or limited experience.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a forward-looking perimeter change rather than an error in the as-filed valuation. The supplied record also contains an unresolved identity mismatch: the valuation names GroGlass, while the 10-Q describes the pending KCI acquisition. Until closing terms and funding are filed for the acquisition actually referenced, the valuation effect cannot be established.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile whether GroGlass and KCI are separate transactions; at each closing obtain the final consideration, financing, assumed liabilities, issued shares, transaction costs, acquired results, and post-close balance sheet, then rerun the valuation.

audit_findings.title: Some cash and short-term investments may not be distributable
audit_findings.magnitude: At least $6.244 million, approximately $0.29 per diluted share and 0.7% of the $861 million base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Collateralized short-term securities included as surplus cash overstate the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The reinsurance carrier requires Prism to maintain fixed-maturity investments, for the purpose of providing collateral for Prism's obligations under the reinsurance agreements.
audit_findings.explanation: The $32.678 million bridge addition equals the latest $26.434 million cash balance plus $6.244 million of current fixed-maturity investments. The filing demonstrates that those investments are held by Prism as required collateral, so adding that $6.244 million as distributable surplus is an error. Removing it would reduce base value from $39.87 to approximately $39.58 per share and would not change the $27.91 buy-below conclusion. Any additional restricted or minimum operating cash remains unquantified.
audit_findings.action: Exclude the $6.244 million collateral balance and reconcile remaining cash by legal entity, restriction, insurance requirement, and minimum operating need; rerun only if additional exclusions become large enough to affect the conclusion.

audit_findings.title: An unfunded pension claim is absent from the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $4.897 million gross underfunded status, approximately $0.23 per diluted share and 0.6% of the $861 million base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: An unfunded defined-benefit obligation is a senior claim that reduces the equity bridge unless already captured elsewhere.
audit_findings.evidence: We also sponsor an unfunded Supplemental Executive Retirement Plan (SERP), a defined-benefit pension plan that was frozen to new entrants in fiscal 2009, with no additional benefits accruing to plan participants after such time.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates a $4.897 million underfunded status and the supplied bridge does not show a pension deduction. Even deducting the full gross amount would reduce base value from $39.87 to approximately $39.64 per share and would not change the buy-below conclusion; tax effects could make the deduction smaller.
audit_findings.action: Confirm that the deficit was not netted elsewhere, update its funded status and tax effect, and include the resulting net claim in the bridge on the next rerun.
